subject: get estimates with predict for an occupancy model with 2 factors

messages.author: fdaa54d30ab7b913
messages.subject: get estimates with predict for an occupancy model with 2 factors
parts:
Dear list members,

Some time ago I asked about an occupancy model with 2 factors (f1 and f2) and Andy and Ian suggested me a work around using linearComb.

Now I want something similar using predict and I am trying the following code to get the estimates for the levels of one factor (site), keeping constant at one level of the second factor (season):

> newData  <-  data.frame(site = factor(c("a", "b", "c"), levels=c("a", "b", "c")), season = factor("c", levels=c("a", "b", "c")))
> p = predict(mod2brid, type="det", newdata=newData, appendData=TRUE)
> p
  Predicted         SE      lower     upper site season
1 0.1769034 0.08032784 0.06794318 0.3878837    a      c
2 0.4658077 0.11468941 0.26108134 0.6827395    b      c
3 0.6848654 0.10457781 0.45673910 0.8488901    c      c

Is that approach correct?

Thank you very much in advance,

Manuel

messages.author: 527e14923215b7e4
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] get estimates with predict for an occupancy model with 2 factors
parts:
Hi Manuel,

Your code looks correct. You can double check things by manipulating the beta coefficients yourself and then back-transforming using the inverse-logit function, (plogis in R).

Also, as a general comment, predict() is simply a wrapper around linearComb(). The differences is that predict creates the design matrix automatically. To see how this works, take a look at the model.matrix function in R.

Richard

messages.author: 527e14923215b7e4
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] get estimates with predict for an occupancy model with 2 factors
parts:
Hi Manuel,

Your code below is correct if you are trying to get predicted values of p for each site at _unique_ values of season. If you are trying to get predictions for each site _averaged_ over the levels of season, then you need to follow Ian and Andy's previous advice. This can be done using either linearComb or predict. If you want to use predict, then  you need to specify custom contrasts. These should be equivalent:

# Predictions of p for each site averaged over seasons
newData  <-  data.frame(site = factor(c("a", "b", "c")),
                        season = factor(c("a", "b", "c")))
contrasts(newData$season) <- matrix(1/3, 3, 2) # define custom contrasts

# Same thing using linearComb
backTransform(linearComb(mod2brid["det"],
    matrix(c(1,0,0,1/3,1/3,
             1,1,0,1/3,1/3,
             1,0,1,1/3,1/3), nrow=3, byrow=TRUE)))

Richard
